items.title: Dietary supplements for treating osteoarthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.summary: Meta-analysis of 69 studies found only 7 of 20 dietary supplements showed efficacy for osteoarthritis, with collagen hydrolysate, passion fruit peel extract, Curcuma longa extract, and Boswellia serrata extract among those with evidence.

items.title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of the Intra-articular Injection of Autologous Adipose-Derived Mesenchymal Stem Cells for Knee Osteoarthritis: A Phase III, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
items.journal: The American journal of sports medicine
items.summary: Phase III randomized trial of intra-articular autologous adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells failed to show significant benefit over placebo for knee osteoarthritis pain and function.

items.title: Effect of Intra-articular Triamcinolone vs Saline on Knee Cartilage Volume and Pain in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: Two-year randomized trial found intra-articular triamcinolone injections every 3 months caused greater cartilage volume loss compared to saline in knee osteoarthritis patients.

items.title: Effect of Intra-Articular Sprifermin vs Placebo on Femorotibial Joint Cartilage Thickness in Patients With Osteoarthritis: The FORWARD Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: FORWARD trial showed sprifermin failed to meet its primary endpoint of increasing femorotibial joint cartilage thickness in knee osteoarthritis patients.

items.title: Effectiveness and safety of glucosamine and chondroitin for the treatment of osteoarthritis: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.journal: Journal of orthopaedic surgery and research
items.summary: Meta-analysis of 30 trials found glucosamine and chondroitin showed minimal to no symptomatic effectiveness for knee and hip osteoarthritis treatment.

items.title: Acetaminophen for osteoarthritis.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
items.summary: Cochrane review found acetaminophen provided only minimal pain relief for osteoarthritis compared to placebo with small effect sizes.

items.title: Stem cell injections for osteoarthritis of the knee.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
items.summary: Cochrane review of stem cell injections for knee osteoarthritis found insufficient evidence of benefits and uncertainty regarding harms.

items.title: Rofecoxib for osteoarthritis.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
items.summary: Cochrane review of rofecoxib for osteoarthritis, noting the drug was withdrawn from market in 2004 due to increased cardiovascular risk with long-term use.

items.title: Physical activity and exercise for chronic pain in adults: an overview of Cochrane Reviews.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
items.summary: Cochrane overview found physical activity and exercise programmes provide benefits for chronic pain conditions including osteoarthritis.

items.title: Effectiveness and safety of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and opioid treatment for knee and hip osteoarthritis: network meta-analysis.
items.summary: Network meta-analysis comparing NSAIDs, opioids, and paracetamol for knee and hip osteoarthritis to determine optimal effectiveness and safety profiles.

items.title: Physical therapy for patients with knee and hip osteoarthritis: supervised, active treatment is current best practice.
items.summary: Expert review emphasizing that supervised exercise therapy and education delivered by physical therapists are core first-line treatments for knee and hip osteoarthritis.

items.title: Risk factors and burden of osteoarthritis.
items.journal: Annals of physical and rehabilitation medicine

items.title: The global burden of hip and knee osteoarthritis: estimates from the global burden of disease 2010 study.

canonicalFacts.claim: Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis and a leading cause of disability in elderly populations
Exercise therapy provides pain relief comparable to pharmacological medications without serious adverse effects
Risk factors for osteoarthritis include age, gender, obesity, genetics, joint injury, and malalignment
Most dietary supplements lack strong evidence for osteoarthritis treatment effectiveness

lifestyleRecommendations.recommendation: Engage in supervised exercise therapy and physical activity programs as first-line treatment
Maintain healthy weight to reduce joint loading and osteoarthritis progression risk
Participate in patient education programs alongside exercise therapy

redFlags: Intra-articular corticosteroids may accelerate cartilage loss with repeated use
Long-term opioid use carries significant risks and limited long-term benefits
Rofecoxib and similar COX-2 inhibitors carry cardiovascular risks
